A. Diamond and graphite - Both are allotropes of carbon. They are made entirely of carbon atoms arranged in different structures. Diamond has a tetrahedral crystal structure, while graphite has a layered structure, but both contain only carbon atoms.

B. Salt and sugar - Salt (sodium chloride, NaCl) contains sodium and chlorine atoms. Sugar (typically sucrose, C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) contains carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen atoms. These substances contain different elements.

C. Sand and chalk - Sand is primarily silicon dioxide (SiO₂), containing silicon and oxygen atoms. Chalk is calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), containing calcium, carbon, and oxygen atoms. These substances contain different elements.

D. Sand and sulfur - Sand is primarily silicon dioxide (SiO₂), containing silicon and oxygen atoms. Sulfur is an element itself (S). These substances contain different elements.
